dedupe_keys.name: china 2021 rainstorm events multi regional indirect economic losses from an adaptive mrio model

description: This study identifies the major rainstorm events in China in 2021, collects the direct economic losses of each, and estimates the indirect losses that spread through interregional trade with an adaptive multi-regional input-output model. Yuan Liu, Ying Li and colleagues at the National Climate Center of the China Meteorological Administration published it in Frontiers in Earth Science in January 2023. China had 36 major rainstorm events in 2021 with about 179.8 billion yuan of direct losses, centred on Henan, Hebei and Shaanxi. The July 2021 Henan flood was the most damaging, with 125.8 billion yuan direct and 269.1 billion yuan indirect losses; Henan's primary industry was hit hard and the effects reached Inner Mongolia and Guangdong. Indirect losses grew non-linearly with direct losses, and a sensitivity test showed moderate overproduction reduces indirect impacts. Coverage is mainland China at provincial level. Format and access: open access article with supplementary material; no model code is released. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the loss model depends on the input-output table year and on reported direct losses. It is a benchmark for resilience and hazard exposure studies of flood ripple effects through supply chains. A related catalogue record is the CEADs multi-regional input-output table collection.
